target_customer: PC gamers paying a monthly subscription; indie developers paid from the pool
problem: Indie games struggled with discoverability and revenue; Dropleaf offered an all-you-can-play subscription.
business_model: Consumer subscription with revenue share to developers

founders.name: Vikram Rangraj
prior_employers: Rize Education (Chief Academic Officer, per YC page)

founders.name: Zi Guo
founders.background_notes: Crunchbase snippet calls Zi Guo co-founder and president.

competitors.name: IndieBox
competitors.what: Indie game collector's edition subscription box
competitors.traction_then: Shipped 40+ collector editions over four years

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed a game launcher, DRM or access control and developer payout tracking, plus catalog deals.

defensibility.rationale: Catalog depended on developer deals and Steam and Humble could run similar offers.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source documents incumbent action; Dropleaf's end is not public.

market_need_then: YC post and GamesBeat 2017 cite indie discoverability problems; launch had 41 games at 4.99 dollars per month.

brand_strength.rationale: Covered by KitGuru, GamesBeat, PC Games Insider and The Mary Sue in 2017 but no brand assets or community evidence found.

outcome_analysis: Dropleaf launched in August 2017 with 41 indie games at 4.99 dollars a month and later sold discounted multi-year subscriptions with 70 plus games. YC lists it Inactive but no shutdown notice, funding record or post-mortem was found, so the cause is not public.
notes: Website dropleaf.io returned 503. No funding found beyond the standard YC deal. IndieBox is an adjacent subscription from an October 2017 article, a few weeks after the batch. Searches showed Zi Guo as a former Microsoft employee in a KitGuru snippet (not opened, so not recorded). Humble Monthly and itch.io not confirmed by a dated source.
